userStories.title: Use Claude Message Batches API for Phase S multi-story validation
userStories.description: Phase S currently validates stories sequentially via individual Claude API calls. Submitting all pending story validation requests as a single Message Batches API request cuts cost by 50% and enables asynchronous processing of up to 10,000 stories per batch, completing in under 1 hour. This also unlocks stacking with prompt caching discounts for further savings.
acceptanceCriteria: Phase S submits a batch of up to SPIRAL_STORY_BATCH_SIZE validation requests to the Message Batches API when batch size > 1
Batch results are polled with exponential backoff until all requests resolve
Single-story runs fall back to the synchronous path transparently
Results file records batch_id for each story attempt row in results.tsv
Unit tests verify batch request construction and response parsing
technicalNotes: POST /v1/messages/batches with up to 10,000 custom_id-keyed requests
Cost is 50% of standard API prices; compatible with prompt caching (discounts stack)

userStories.title: Add episodic memory store for Ralph workers to recall past implementation patterns
userStories.description: Research on AI agent memory (arxiv:2512.13564) categorizes agent memory into working, episodic, and semantic forms. SPIRAL's Ralph workers have no episodic memory â€” each worker begins every story without knowledge of how similar stories were implemented in prior iterations. Writing a compact episodic record of 'story type â†’ implementation approach â†’ outcome' to a SQLite FTS5 store and injecting the top-3 relevant past implementations into Ralph's context provides few-shot learning from SPIRAL's own history.
acceptanceCriteria: A .spiral/episodic_memory.db SQLite database stores records with columns: story_id, story_type, approach_summary, outcome (pass/fail), iteration, timestamp
After each successful Ralph execution, lib/impl/commit_revert.sh writes a summary (generated by a cheap haiku call) to the episodic store
Before Ralph executes a story, the top-3 most similar past implementations (by story title keyword match or FTS5 similarity) are retrieved and injected as few-shot examples in the user message
A spiral memory list command displays the 20 most recent episodic records with their pass/fail outcomes
technicalNotes: Use SQLite with FTS5 (full-text search) for keyword-based retrieval without an embedding model dependency. For semantic similarity, optionally integrate with a local embedding (e.g., nomic-embed-text via ollama) gated by SPIRAL_EPISODIC_EMBEDDINGS=true.
The episodic record injection should be placed after the static system prompt but before the story description, to avoid invalidating the cached prompt prefix.
userStories._failureReason: story_too_large_for_single_invocation â€” manually decomposed into 4 sub-stories after 7+ failed attempts across haiku/sonnet/opus; each sub-story is scoped to 1-2 files
_antiPatterns: Attempting all 4 components in one invocation â€” always exceeds 100 tool call budget
Reading full ralph.sh (2800+ lines) without a grep anchor â€” burns 10+ tool calls on navigation alone

userStories.title: Derive cross-iteration story velocity model from results.tsv to improve cost estimates
userStories.description: SPIRAL's python main.py estimate command uses static per-story cost estimates. results.tsv accumulates per-story telemetry (model, tokens, cost, duration, status) across all iterations, providing a growing empirical dataset for velocity and cost forecasting. Fitting a simple linear regression on story_type to (mean_tokens, mean_duration, pass_rate) from results.tsv enables estimate to produce data-driven projections that improve as SPIRAL runs more iterations.
acceptanceCriteria: python main.py estimate reads results.tsv and groups rows by a story_type heuristic (derived from story title keywords or tags)
For each story type with at least 5 historical data points, the estimate uses the empirical mean cost and duration; otherwise falls back to the static default
python main.py estimate --report outputs a table showing: story_type, historical_samples, mean_tokens, mean_cost, empirical_pass_rate, estimated_retries
The model is saved to .spiral/velocity_model.json on each estimate run so it persists between sessions
technicalNotes: Use scipy.stats.linregress or numpy polyfit for the regression. For classification of story types, use simple keyword matching on the title (e.g., 'Add OTel' -> 'observability', 'Fix bug' -> 'bug_fix') rather than a model call.
Consider a rolling window (last 50 rows per story type) rather than all historical data to account for model upgrades that change token patterns.

userStories.title: Extract repeated spiral CI steps into composite actions in .github/actions/
userStories.description: SPIRAL's CI has multiple workflow files that repeat setup steps: checkout, uv setup, Python version matrix, shellcheck, shfmt. Converting these into composite actions stored in .github/actions/ reduces duplication, makes SHA-pinned action updates apply in one place, and follows the GitHub Actions 2025 best practice of separating shared task templates from pipeline templates.
acceptanceCriteria: A .github/actions/setup-uv/action.yml composite action handles Python setup, uv install, and cache restore
A .github/actions/lint-shell/action.yml composite action encapsulates shellcheck and shfmt steps
All existing workflow files are updated to call these composite actions with no raw duplicated steps remaining
CI passes after the migration; SHA-pinned versions of third-party actions are defined only in the composite actions
technicalNotes: Composite actions run inline in the calling job with no separate job overhead
Secrets must be passed explicitly as inputs â€” composite actions do not inherit secrets automatically

userStories.title: Export Prometheus metrics from results.tsv for real-time cost monitoring
userStories.description: Add `/metrics` endpoint to the self-monitoring dashboard that exposes phase-level token burn rate, per-story cost, and model distribution as Prometheus-compatible metrics. Parse results.tsv every 5 seconds and compute rolling window (last 10 iterations) for live cost tracking.
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard server at localhost:5299/metrics returns metrics in Prometheus text format: spiral_tokens_total{phase=<phase>,model=<model>}, spiral_cost_usd{story_id=<id>}, spiral_iteration_duration_seconds

lib/metrics_exporter.py exports parse_results_tsv() function that returns dict with cumulative tokens/cost per phase and per story from last N iterations (configurable via SPIRAL_METRICS_WINDOW, default 10)

Metrics update at least every 5 seconds during active iteration (verified by timestamp header in /metrics response). Cost ceiling warnings trigger at 50%, 80%, 95% thresholds with metric labels cost_ceiling_pct={threshold}
